text:
morgan: Quick question — where should we document/own timeout & abort semantics across SDKs? e.g., AbortController in JS, context.Context in Go, signals in Python. Do we align on default behavior or let each SDK decide? :thinking:

tess: My take: SDKs should provide consistent user-facing semantics: immediate cancel of streaming, and a clear signal to the runtime to stop work when feasible. But defaults can vary (client short default vs server longer SLO). We need a doc + tests.

zach: +1. Also need clarified retry behavior when request is cancelled mid-stream. Should retries happen automatically? I think only on idempotent/non-streaming endpoints.

lin: From the runtime perspective, client disconnects are advisory by default; we don't automatically kill GPU runs mid-inference unless an explicit cancel request is received. Killing mid-run can be expensive and unsafe for pooled resources.

morgan: Ok — proposal for triage: 
- Client abort => SDK emits abort signal to transport and cancels local resources immediately (streams close, no local retry).
- Server/runtime => interprets client disconnect as advisory; model run may continue unless an explicit cancel endpoint/header is used.
- Retries => only for non-streaming idempotent APIs; streaming retries must be opt-in and handled by application.

tess: Can we add example ergonomics? Node uses AbortController: 
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
client.generate(..., { signal: ac.signal });
// later
ac.abort(); // should close stream and drop receiving tokens
```
Python should surface asyncio cancellations / CancelledError and support a `timeout=` param for sync calls: 
```py
async with client.stream(...) as s:
    try:
        await s.receive()
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        # SDK should teardown stream and close connection
        pass
```

zach: Test needs: ensure that abort triggers stream end event, underlying TCP connection closed, and no dangling GPU tasks. We should add an integration that asserts runtime job ended or has explicit cancel record within Xs.

morgan: I'll open a design doc + PR for the SDK API convention and tests. cc @tess @lin for API shape. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412 — please review when you have cycles.

deploy-bot: morgan's PR 412 checks passed. :white_check_mark:

tess: Quick note for JS SDK review — ensure abort doesn't trigger the automatic retry wrapper (we currently wrap fetch in retry logic). I'll add a unit test that simulates AbortError and asserts no retry attempts.

lin: I'll sync with runtime team and propose an `x-explicit-cancel: true` header or a separate cancel RPC so we can safely terminate running models. Will update runtime issue after that sync.

morgan: Can someone add a short 'what happens when your request is aborted' section to the SDK README with examples? Assigning to @tess.

tess: On it, targeting EOD tomorrow.

zach: Tagging this for next week's devex async Q&A slot in case folks want a deeper dive or to see the PR walkthrough.

morgan: Thanks all — we'll merge when tests are green and runtime has a cancel plan.
